Court Street runs along the top edge, Washington Street and Park Place along the right edge, and De Hart Street along the bottom, with Ann Street and Maple Avenue crossing from top to bottom on the left. Bank Street and Market Street run obliquely across the middle and enclose a narrow triangular block at the left, where they diverge from one another. The right-hand side is a continuous row of brick and frame stores and offices facing Washington Street and Park Place, among them the Masonic Hall, the Banner building, the Morristown Trust Co., the Telephone Exchange, Pipers Hotel, the 1st National Bank, the American Trust Co. and the Young Men's Catholic Association rooms, with Piper Lane and Schmidt's Lane giving rear access. Block 282 holds several garages, notably Dutton's Garage and a Ford service station with an auto hotel. The public school stands between Maple Avenue and Schmidt's Lane in block 267, next to the De Hart Street garage and Stevenson's garage. West of Ann Street the blocks are much thinner, with dwellings, livery stables, a city yard, the Armstrong Garage, wagon shops and small manufactories along Bank Street, and open ground behind them. Granville Alley is a private way north of Bank Street. Water pipes with sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets, and the sheet's own compass rose stands in the open ground at upper left.
notes: Court, Ann, Bank, Market, Washington and South are Court Street, Ann Street, Bank Street, Market Street, Washington Street and South Street in OpenStreetMap; De Hart is Dehart Street.
The street along the right edge printed Park Pl. is West Park Place and North Park Place today.
Schmidt's Lane, Piper Lane and Granville Alley are not named streets in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Downtown west of the Green: Court, Ann, Bank, Market, Maple, Dehart; north about +45.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the north-western side of the Morristown business district and the residential blocks above it, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Washington Street crosses the left half diagonally from Atno Avenue at upper left to Park Place at the foot of the sheet, with Prospect Street running down the right side and Clinton Street cut off along the top edge. High Street crosses the middle between Washington and Prospect. The upper half is a block of dwellings, mostly two-storey frame houses with small outbuildings, with Oliver Lane, a narrow lane, running down through block 291; the First Baptist Church, drawn in blue, stands on Washington Street at High Street, and a boarding house stands to its north. Below High Street the sheet changes character to a dense commercial block, number 290, bounded by Washington Street, High Street, Speedwell Avenue and Park Place. Along its edges are brick and frame stores, garages, a barber, a plumber, restaurants, a shoe shop, the Elks Club and the United States Hotel, and at the right the long McAlpin Block, with a department store at its southern corner. The middle of the block is the McAlpin Estate general storage warehouses, with a livery building, a hatching shed and a stone retaining wall. Park Place and the Park, as the Green is lettered, appear at the bottom, and Water Street leaves at lower right. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets, and street widths of 50 and 66 feet are given. Neighbouring sheet numbers are printed in the margins.
notes: High is Cattano Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Clinton, Washington, Prospect and Park Place are Clinton Street, Washington Street, Prospect Street and West Park Place or North Park Place.
Oliver Lane is not a street in OpenStreetMap.
Court Street meets Washington Street about 5 m closer to High Street in OpenStreetMap than on the sheet.
50 ft. NW of the Green: Atno, Washington, High (= Cattano Avenue), Prospect, Speedwell; rotation +36.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the north-eastern edge of Morristown's centre, where Speedwell Avenue runs diagonally across the sheet from upper left to lower right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper left. Spring Street crosses the top, Prospect Street and High Street the lower left, and Water Street the right edge, while Clinton Place runs along the upper left side of the lower-left block. Speedwell Avenue is lined on both sides with a continuous row of small shops: groceries, a fruit seller, a tailor, restaurants, a bowling alley and pool room, a laundry, saloons, jewellers, undertakers and a harness maker, mostly in frame and some in brick. The Palace Theatre, a brick building with a stage and scenery space, stands on the west side near High Street. The street ends at the lower right in a triangular lot occupied by the fire patrol, hook and ladder truck, engine company and police headquarters. Behind the shops on the west side lie blocks of detached frame dwellings, drawn with their porches and outbuildings, in blocks 292 and 19. At the upper right a brook crosses the sheet and a group of dwellings, a few shops and vacant lots fills the angle between Spring Street and Water Street, reached by Mill Lane. A small pond is drawn at the left. Large parts of the sheet are left blank where the streets are drawn on neighbouring sheets, and block numbers 15, 19, 2 and 4 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Prospect, Spring and Water are Prospect Street, Spring Street and Water Street in OpenStreetMap; High is Cattano Avenue.
Mill Lane is not a street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Speedwell Avenue, Spring, Clinton Place, Prospect, High (= Cattano Avenue); 4 points.

sheet-4-1.description: Sheet 4 part 1 covers the area north-east and east of the Morristown Green, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Spring Street runs down the middle from top to bottom, ending at Morris Street along the foot of the sheet; Center Street crosses it near the middle and runs east over an iron and concrete bridge across the Whippany River, which sweeps in a curve across the upper right. Water Street runs diagonally across the top, and again down the left side from the upper centre to Park Place at lower left. The block between Water Street and Spring Street is largely open ground holding the Public Service Gas Co. works, with a gasometer marked not used and a warehouse, while the east side of Center Street carries the No. 1 gasometer, capacity 207,000 cubic feet, in block 304. A large cemetery fills the open centre of the left half, with the First Presbyterian Church, its chapel and manse, drawn in blue, at its southern edge, and the Park Theatre, Park Apartments and a row of shops lining Water Street at lower left. Along Spring Street stand frame dwellings and shops, the Bethel A.M.E. Church, the Union Baptist Church rooms, the Morris Hat Manufacturing Co. and a row of small shops on Morris Street. Spring Place leads off to the east. At upper right are dwellings, a lumber yard and a junk yard along Water Street. The upper left corner is an inset, not included in this part, showing the Morristown Memorial Hospital at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Spring, Center, Morris and Water are Spring Street, Center Street, Morris Street and Water Street in OpenStreetMap; the street lettered Water along the top of the sheet is Martin Luther King Avenue today.
The crossing of Center Street and Spring Street drawn on the sheet was matched to the OpenStreetMap node shared by Center, Spring and Water streets.
The part rests on two hand-picked junctions, so its scale and rotation are low confidence.
Part 1 main, 50 ft (Spring, Center, Water = Martin Luther King Avenue, Morris), two hand-picked points (helmert); part 2 inset Memorial Hospital, 100 ft, unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Morristown Memorial Hospital, 100 ft (no street junction in OSM on the inset; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-13 or sheet-4-1).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential district south-west of Morristown's business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Dehart Street runs along the top, Maple Avenue down the middle, MacCulloch Avenue along the left edge, South Street along the right edge and Miller Road across the lower part, with Oak Street meeting Maple Avenue from the west. West of Maple Avenue the blocks, numbered 261 and 262, are filled with detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, a few with auto sheds, and one brick garage in pink. East of Maple Avenue the blocks hold more dwellings, a boarding house and the Red Cross headquarters, and, in block 260, the South Street Presbyterian Church with its Sunday school rooms, a manse and the Public Library, a fire-resistive building drawn in blue. At the northeast corner, facing Dehart Street and South Street, is a small commercial group: a milk depot, sewing machines, plumbing, a photographer, a druggist, furrier, tailor, news stand and a phonograph parlor, with L. M. Christensen Inc., cleaning and dyeing, whose plant carries a gasoline tank and benzine house, on a lane behind them. South of Miller Road, in blocks 234 and 230, stand more dwellings and, at the right, St. Peter's Episcopal Church with its tower, rectory and parish house, drawn in blue. The sheet's compass rose stands in a vacant lot at upper left. Water pipes with sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets, and the street widths of 50 and 66 feet are given.
notes: Dehart, Oak, South and Miller Road are Dehart Street, Oak Street, South Street and Miller Road in OpenStreetMap; Macculloch Avenue is MacCulloch Avenue.
Miller Road is lettered with the alternative name Boyken in parentheses.
50 ft. Dehart, Maple, Oak, Miller Rd, MacCulloch, South.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers a mixed commercial and residential district between the Morristown Green and Pine Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. South Street runs along the foot of the sheet, Park Place down the left side and Pine Street down the right, with Morris Street curving round the top and left of a fan-shaped group of blocks and Dumont Place crossing the middle from lower left to Pine Street. Blatchley Place and Wilmot Street lead into the blocks from Morris Street and Dumont Place. The curve of Morris Street is lined with small shops: groceries, a confectioner, a cleaner and dyer, a barber, a tailor, a plumber, awnings and warehouses. Along Morris Street to the upper right stand dwellings and, at the top, a large garage for forty cars. In the middle are tenements, the George A. Mills Wood Working Co. with its lumber shed and sash, door and blind factory, a carpenter shop and a junk yard. The post office, drawn in orange and marked fire proof, built in 1917, stands on the west side of the fan. Along Park Place and South Street are the Daily Record printing office, the M. E. Church with its Sunday school and parsonage, the Church of the Redeemer with its rectory and parish house, the National Iron Bank, a lodge, the Armory, auto repairing and show rooms. Wiss Bros garage for sixty cars and Robt Elliott, florist, with its greenhouses, stand beside Dumont Place near Pine Street. A site marked ruins lies beside the Armory. Block numbers 4, 12, 11, 5 and 1 mark the neighbouring sheets.
notes: Morris, Pine, South, Dumont and King are Morris Street, Pine Street, South Street, Dumont Place and King Place in OpenStreetMap; Wilmot Street is a service road there and Blatchley Place is not an OpenStreetMap street.
De Hart Street is Dehart Street in OpenStreetMap.
The part rests on five detected junctions, mostly along Dumont Place and Pine Street, and its leave-one-out error is about 5 m.
50 ft. Morris, Dumont Pl (Wilmot St a service way), Pine, South, Park Pl; rotation -49.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows a strip of residential Morristown south-west of the business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper right. Colles Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, and MacCulloch Avenue forms the right-hand edge. Wetmore Avenue crosses at the top, Farragut Place in the upper middle, and Miller Road, with the name Boyken added in parentheses, near the foot, so that blocks 251 and 263 and the north side of block 236 are shown. East of Colles Avenue the blocks are filled with detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, nearly all with small outbuildings or auto sheds behind them, and a few brick or brick-veneer houses are coloured pink; two larger pink buildings stand near MacCulloch Avenue. West of Colles Avenue the ground is much emptier: a large open tract in block 251 with a few small buildings, and a row of dwellings along the north side of Miller Road. A compass rose and north arrow are printed at the upper left. Water pipes of four inches run in the streets, with hydrants and numbered circles giving the street elevation at each crossing, and street widths of 50 and 66 feet are marked. The numbers of the adjoining sheets are printed in the margins, 8 above, 9 below and 20 to the left.
notes: Miller Road is printed with the name Boyken in parentheses; OpenStreetMap names it Miller Road.
MacCulloch is printed only as a vertical label at the right edge of the sheet, partly cut by the scan edge; its junctions with Farragut Place and Miller Road lie on the edge.
50 ft. Colles Av, Wetmore, Farragut, Miller Rd (Boyken); MacCulloch Av on the right edge.

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 8 is the lower and right-hand part of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper right. It lies at the north-west edge of the built-up town, between Colles Avenue on the left and MacCulloch Avenue on the right, with Wetmore Avenue along the foot and Mount Kemble Avenue crossing the middle. Entrance Avenue runs north-east from Mount Kemble Avenue towards the upper right, its upper stretch labelled Terrace Place in parentheses. Along the north side of Mount Kemble Avenue stand rows of frame dwellings on narrow deep lots, and between Mount Kemble and Wetmore Avenues are the blocks numbered 250 and 256 with more frame houses. Near Entrance Avenue is the Old Ladies Home, a group of pink brick buildings with frame wings, and several detached dwellings stand on large lots around it. Much of the left-hand side of the part is open land crossed by faint dashed lines of unbuilt streets, including an unnamed way running up from Mount Kemble Avenue. The upper left of the sheet is a separate inset at 100 feet to an inch (Burnham Park, Mendham Road) and is cut out of this part by a heavy line that runs along the top of the area and up the right side. A compass rose and north arrow are at the top right, and water pipes, hydrants and street widths are marked in the streets.
notes: Mount Kemble Avenue and Entrance Avenue are named the same in OpenStreetMap.
Court at the top right and De Hart at the right edge are partly cut by the scan edge; Court is read at low confidence.
The 100 ft inset at the top left of the sheet (part 2) is not georeferenced.
Part 1 main 50 ft (Colles, Mt Kemble, Entrance, MacCulloch, Wetmore); part 2 inset top left (Burnham Park, Mendham Road), 100 ft, unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Burnham Park, Mendham Road and Washington Street, 100 ft (no confirmed junction; needs a junction with sheet-25 or carried points).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the south-western edge of residential Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper right. MacCulloch Avenue forms the right-hand edge of the sheet. Madison and James Streets run in from it towards the left and Green Street joins them, so that the blocks numbered 235 and 236 and the street frontage along Madison Street are the only closely built ground. Along Madison Street, from MacCulloch Avenue to about Green Street, stand a continuous row of frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys with sheds behind, with a single pink brick house, and a similar but looser row lines the north side of James Street. Between them, the block bounded by Madison, Green and James Streets has more dwellings and a large open yard. North of Madison Street and west of Green Street the sheet is mostly open land cut by long dashed lot lines, with a few detached dwellings and several auto sheds near the middle of the upper half, and the lower left corner has a small group of buildings on an unnamed road. Perry Street is printed in the upper right where it meets MacCulloch Avenue. A compass rose is at the upper left. Four-inch water pipes, hydrants and elevation circles are marked in the streets, and street widths of 50 and 56 feet are given.
notes: Madison, James and Green are Madison Street, James Street and Green Street in OpenStreetMap.

Green Street is left out of the georeferencing control: its modern line is about 4 m from the drawn street at its junctions with James and Madison Streets, so the sheet is placed from MacCulloch Avenue alone.
Perry Street is printed in the upper right where it meets MacCulloch Avenue.
50 ft. Madison, James, Green; placed from MacCulloch Av only (helmert); Green St left out (4 m residuals).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers four blocks of residential Morristown south-west of the business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It is bounded by MacCulloch Avenue along the left edge and South Street along the right, with Perry, Madison and James streets crossing between them and Maple Avenue running through the middle. Catherine Lane, a narrow lane, divides the block between Madison and James west of Maple Avenue. The block between Perry and Madison west of Maple is dominated by the Roman Catholic Church of the Assumption with its sexton's house and rectory, and by St. Mary's School and a sisters' house, all drawn in brick. The remaining blocks are filled with frame dwellings, many of two or two and a half storeys, with small auto sheds behind them; several garages and auto repair shops show the spread of the motor car, among them the carriage and auto repairing works of B. M. Tunis facing South Street and a garage on Maple Avenue. A boarding house named The Pasadena stands on South Street. South of James Street the sheet is mostly open ground in block 140, with the club house and men's and women's lockers of the Morristown Field Club near South Street. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets, and the street widths of 50 and 66 feet are given at the edges.
notes: Macculloch Avenue is MacCulloch Avenue in OpenStreetMap; South, Perry, Madison and James are South Street, Perry Street, Madison Street and James Street.
Church of the Assumption (R.C.) and St. Mary's School occupy the block between Perry and Madison west of Maple Avenue.
50 ft. Perry, Madison, James between MacCulloch Av and South St, Maple Av; Church of the Assumption, St. Mary's School. Pilot sheet: defaults, 8 points, RMSE 0.88 m.

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper right. It covers the district south-east of the Morristown Green between Pine Street along the top and Madison and Elm Streets along the bottom. South Street runs as a wide diagonal on the left, with Miller Road beside the heavy line that closes off the inset at the upper left. King Place and King Street bound the right-hand side, and Franklin Street and Altamont Court run south from Elm Street at the foot. Along Pine Street at the top are rows of frame dwellings and the Morristown Inn, a large building facing a lawn. In the middle is a wide open block numbered 224 holding a fireproof building marked as built in 1918, the Morristown Club in pink at its west end, and the greenhouses of the Thos. Holton Est. Florist. A line of dwellings and small shops faces South Street, and along Elm Street east of Madison Street runs a row of frame houses with outbuildings. Between Elm Street and the bottom edge, the blocks numbered 150, 33 and 172 hold large dwellings in generous grounds. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the left centre. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50 and 66 feet are marked.
notes: The modern South Street and the junction of Madison, Elm and South Streets lie about 40 m from the drawn junction, so South and Madison Streets are not used for control.
The inset at the upper left (part 2) is the Electrical Alloy Co. works on Ridgedale Avenue, belonging to the area of sheet 35.

Part 1 main 50 ft (Elm, Franklin, King Pl, Pine; Madison/South junction left out, modern node about 40 m off); part 2 inset Electrical Alloy Co. at Ridgedale Av / John St, anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is a block at the upper left of the sheet, closed off from the main map by a heavy line on the right and along the foot, and printed with the number 35 beside its principal building because it continues on sheet 35. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left, with its own compass rose at the left. It shows the works of the Electrical Alloy Co., a large machine shop of pink brick with a raised skylight roof, a dryer room, an office, a shipping room and a lumber shed, with a night watchman's clock system and hose stations described in the lettering above. A side track of the Morristown and Erie Railroad runs along the south side of the works, and a high bank and a rough road lie to the east. Ridgedale Avenue runs down the left of the part and John Street crosses at the foot. A garage with a cement floor stands at the top of the part. Water pipes of six inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants and a numbered street-elevation circle at the Ridgedale and John Street crossing, and the width of Ridgedale Avenue is marked as 66 feet.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point at the Ridgedale Avenue and John Street crossing, with scale from the main map and rotation from the north arrow and Ridgedale Avenue; low confidence.

Part 1 main 50 ft (Elm, Franklin, King Pl, Pine; Madison/South junction left out, modern node about 40 m off); part 2 inset Electrical Alloy Co. at Ridgedale Av / John St, anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the centre of the town's south-eastern business edge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper right. Pine Street runs across the top, King Street across the upper middle, and Elm Street, the main street, crosses at about two thirds of the height. King Place runs along the left edge, Altamont Court and Hill Street run south from Elm Street, and Morris Street forms the right-hand edge with Blachley Place leaving it in a curve. Rows of frame dwellings face Pine and King Streets. Along the right side stands the commercial strip: H. C. Holmes Florist greenhouses and a garage on Morris Street, shops, a barber, grocer, confectioner, restaurant, electrician, undertaker, cobbler and laundry in a row, and a pink brick storage and van company with a blue cement-walled warehouse beside Blachley Place. South of Elm Street stand The Boyken, a large boarding house in grounds, and the lumber yard and builders' supply yard of C. W. Ennis and Co., served by a siding off the Lackawanna railroad, whose tracks run diagonally down the right edge. Block numbers 223 and 224 lie between Pine, King and Elm Streets, and 170, 171 and 215 to the south. A compass rose stands in the middle of block 224. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 40, 50 and 66 feet are marked.
notes: Drive is the printed name of two short lanes in the commercial block north of Elm Street.
The curve of Blachley Place and the rail yard near Morris Street differ from the modern straight street and tracks.
50 ft. Pine, King, Elm, Hill, Altamont Ct, Morris, Blachley Pl; Lackawanna tracks at right.

sheet-13-1.description: The main part of sheet 13 shows the railroad district east of Morris Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Morris Street runs down the left edge and Olyphant Place along the bottom, continuing to the right as Olyphant Drive; Jardine Road loops up from Olyphant Drive to the Parkway at the right edge, and Lackawanna Place runs diagonally beside the tracks. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right with its fireproof reinforced concrete passenger depot and covered concrete platforms, a freight depot at the head of the freight yard in the upper left, and an express office. To the right lie the yards of the Morristown and Erie Railroad with its passenger depot, freight house, locomotive house and machine shop, a coal bin and a water tank, and the Whippany River runs down the upper right corner. Between the railroads and Olyphant Place are lumber and fuel dealers: C. W. Ennis and Co. Yard No. 2 with its lumber sheds, the Reeve and Burr woodworking mill with a steam dry kiln, the feed and straw store of C. L. Lade, the cold storage plant of Swift and Co., an ice storage house and the coal shed of the Consumers Coal Co. The Washington Hotel stands on Olyphant Place near Morris Street, and frame dwellings line Olyphant Place and the blocks along Jardine Road. The upper part of the sheet carries two insets, the Lackawanna round house and a continuation of Jardine Road, which are separate parts.
notes: Parkway is Olyphant Parkway in OpenStreetMap; Morris is Morris Street.
Lackawanna Place has been realigned since 1918 and Lafayette Avenue now runs through the former yards; neither was used for control.
Placed from Morris Street / Olyphant Place (detected) and two hand-picked junctions on Jardine Road (curved junctions the detector skips).

Three parts: 1 main (DL&W station and freight yard, M&E yards, Olyphant Pl, Jardine Rd, Parkway = Olyphant Parkway; Lackawanna Pl realigned, not used); 2 inset DL&W round house at Pocahontas Lake (north up); 3 inset Jardine Rd north of the Parkway (north to the right). sheet-13-3.description: This small inset in the upper right corner of sheet 13 continues Jardine Road beyond the Parkway, where the main map is cut off by the sheet edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch but turned so that north points to the right, so Jardine Road, which runs roughly north from the Parkway, crosses the inset from left to right. The Parkway leaves Jardine Road downward at the left of the inset. The inset shows parts of blocks 212 and 213: a few frame dwellings on narrow lots north of Jardine Road, the lot lines of the block to the south, a hydrant at the corner of the Parkway and a four-inch water pipe in Jardine Road. Its left edge borders the sidings of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad drawn in the round house inset. The rest of the inset is open ground.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the north-eastern fringe of Morristown on the Whippany River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper right. Abbet Avenue runs from the top of the sheet down to the river, crossing it on a steel bridge, with Lincoln Street, Roosevelt Street and New Street crossing it on the north bank, Garfield Street on the left and Garden Street on the right. The area north of the river is thinly built: a few rows of frame dwellings with sheds on Lincoln Street and Abbet Avenue, and otherwise long narrow lots in the blocks numbered 203, 310, 311 and 313, with Roosevelt Street laid out but unbuilt. The Leonard Hygiene Ice Co. plant stands on the river bank at the foot of Abbet Avenue, with a tank room and concrete floors. South of the Whippany River, which winds across the sheet from left to right, the Morristown and Erie Railroad runs along the bank, and an industrial group stands on either side of Abbet Avenue: the Morris County Coal Co., the Arthur Pierson Tile Works with its long cement-floored sheds, The Texas Co. oil depot and the Standard Oil Co. with oil tanks. Jardine Road and Olyphant Lane curve along the foot, with Erie printed along the bottom edge. A compass rose is at the upper right.
notes: Abbet Avenue is Abbett Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Lincoln, Garfield, New and Garden are Lincoln Street, Garfield Street, New Street and Garden Street there.
Roosevelt Street was laid out but is not in OpenStreetMap; it does not appear to have been built.
Olyphant Lane is Olyphant Drive in OpenStreetMap.
Erie is read at low confidence; it is printed along the bottom edge.
50 ft. Abbett Av, Lincoln, Garfield, New, Garden, Whippany River; control only north of the river; Roosevelt St not in OSM.

sheet-15-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 15 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points a little to the right of the top. It covers the west side of Morristown along Speedwell Avenue, which runs down the left edge to a fork where Spring Street leaves to the south-east. Flagler Street comes in from the left, bends into a long diagonal that cuts the sheet from upper left to lower right and meets Water Street along the foot; Race Street, Chatham, Victor and River streets and Roosevelt Place run off it toward the Whippany River on the right. A strip of the river and the Chuldwell Play Grounds fill the right edge. The blocks are a mix of frame dwellings and denser commercial and tenement property: a row of long brick and frame tenements on the diagonal, a bakery, a neighbourhood house, groceries, barber and meat shops, a large garage with a capacity of sixty cars on Speedwell Avenue, the West End Hotel, feed and shed buildings, a milk depot, and an electric motor and bottling works at the foot of River Street. Open lots and long narrow lots divide the blocks between Spring and Flagler streets. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets, with street widths of 30, 35, 40 and 65 feet. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the upper right. The bottom-left corner of the sheet is a separate inset of Willow Street, cut out of this part by a heavy line.
notes: Printed Chuldwell Play Grounds is spelled as printed.

Speedwell Avenue, Flagler Street, Spring Street and Early Street survive under these names in OpenStreetMap. Water Street, Race, Chatham, Victor and River streets, Marinaro, Nicholas Avenue and Roosevelt Place have no counterpart in the OpenStreetMap network here; the diagonal part of Flagler Street and the river bank were rebuilt as Clyde Potts Drive and Martin Luther King Avenue.
Only three junctions on Speedwell Avenue could be used, so the placement rests on points along one street (low confidence at the right-hand side).
50 ft. Part 1 main (Speedwell Av, Flagler, Spring, Water, Race, River), two-point helmert; part 2 inset Willow St (bottom left), unplaced. Water St area rebuilt as MLK Av / Clyde Potts Drive.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows the part of Morristown between Water Street and Evergreen Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. The Whippany River winds down the left side beside the Chuldwell Play Grounds, with a concrete footbridge across it, and the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western railroad runs as a wide bundle of tracks up the middle of the sheet, crossed by a steel bridge carrying Evergreen Avenue. West of the tracks are River Street, Cole Avenue and Water Street with Roosevelt Place and Victor Street, frame houses, the printing shop of J. H. Hendershot and Son, and the Public Service Gas Company works marked not in operation, with its gasometer at the foot. Beside the tracks stand the Shelley Hygiene Ice Company, with its forty-ton ice machine, and the feed mill and grain elevator of Carpenter and Knight. East of the tracks Willow Street runs north from Evergreen Avenue past the coal, wood and building-material yards of the H. P. Witte Coal Company, while George Street runs south across open ground. Mt. Airy Place and Liberty Street meet at the top right, near a Baptist Church (Negro) on Evergreen Avenue, and Lincoln Street and Garfield Street appear at the lower right. A compass rose and north arrow are at the upper left. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets.
notes: Evergreen Avenue is Martin Luther King Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Cole Avenue matches the modern Coal Avenue; Mount Airy Place, Liberty Street, Willow Street, George Street, Lincoln Street, Garfield Street and Center Street keep their names.
Printed Chuldwell Play Grounds is spelled as printed.
The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western tracks are the Morristown Line; the steel bridge carries Evergreen Avenue over them.
50 ft. Evergreen Av (= Martin Luther King Avenue), Willow, George, Mt Airy Pl, Liberty, Lincoln, Water, Cole Av (= Coal Avenue), Center; DL&W tracks and Whippany River.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the Liberty Street district of Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Evergreen Avenue crosses the lower half of the sheet from lower left to right, and Linden Street and Hazel Street run up from it to the top of the sheet. Liberty Street crosses between them, and Grove Street appears twice at the top. The blocks between Linden and Hazel streets hold the Liberty Street Public School, drawn in pink brick with heating by steam and lighting by electricity, and a row of frame dwellings on long narrow lots facing Evergreen Avenue. Along Hazel Street and on the left of Linden Street the houses are mostly two-storey frame dwellings with small auto sheds, and a marble cutting works stands near the right edge by Hillairy Avenue. South of Evergreen Avenue are Abbet Avenue at the left and Garden Street near the centre, with a few frame houses, a concrete shed and open ground, and the lower right of the sheet is part of Evergreen Cemetery, left blank. Hillairy Avenue runs down the right edge. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the upper right. Water pipes, hydrants, fire alarm boxes and street widths of 35, 50 and 65 feet are marked in the streets.
notes: Evergreen Avenue is Martin Luther King Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Abbet Avenue is Abbett Avenue today. Liberty, Linden, Hazel, Garden and Hillairy keep their names (Linden Street, Liberty Street, Hazel Street, Garden Street, Hillairy Avenue).
Orientation: the sheet is turned about 55 degrees, so Evergreen Avenue runs across the page although it runs north-north-east on the ground.
50 ft. Liberty, Linden, Hazel, Grove, Evergreen Av (= MLK Av), Abbett Av, Garden, Hillairy Av.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows the Collinsville district in the north-east of Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Evergreen Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right near the middle, and Jersey Avenue and Erin Avenue run up from it to the top, with Emmet Avenue along the right edge. Short Street is lettered along the top edge. South of Evergreen Avenue, Walker Street ends at a small block, Monroe Street runs diagonally down to the south-east, and Walnut Street and Cleveland Avenue enclose a block of frame dwellings across which the name Collinsville is spread. A dash-dot line labelled Boundary Line, Morris Township runs diagonally from the lower left to the top, crossing Evergreen and Jersey avenues. Most of the north side is blank, with long narrow lots between Jersey and Erin avenues and a large unbuilt block at the upper right numbered 330, and a few dwellings and a brick house stand along Jersey Avenue. The Collinsville Fire Headquarters, with its chemical extinguishers, stands by Erin Avenue, and the Morris Township Public School, heated by furnace and lit by electricity, stands at the foot on Cleveland Avenue. The lower left is part of Evergreen Cemetery. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the upper right. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 40 to 70 feet are marked.
notes: Evergreen Avenue is Martin Luther King Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Emmet Avenue is Emmett Avenue today. Jersey Avenue, Erin Avenue, Walker Street, Monroe Street, Cleveland Avenue and Walnut Street keep their names.
The dash-dot line is the boundary between Morristown and Morris Township (a town boundary line is also drawn on sheet 19).
50 ft. Jersey, Erin, Emmet, Walker, Monroe, Walnut, Cleveland Avs, Evergreen Av (= MLK Av); Collinsville.

sheet-19-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 19 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north roughly up the page. It lies on the south-west side of the centre of Morristown between Atno Avenue along the left edge and Speedwell Avenue along the right, with Early Street running along the top. Clinton Street and Clinton Place cross the sheet as one long diagonal from the lower left to the Speedwell Avenue business block at the right, and Prospect Street leaves it to the south-east near the middle. A brook enters from the left and runs up beside the lots to a pond below Early Street. The upper part is a long row of frame dwellings on narrow lots facing Early Street and Atno Avenue, with sheds, auto buildings and a wood-working and sash and blind factory. Along Clinton Street stand rows of three-storey frame dwellings, and the right edge is taken up by the Palace Building and other brick shops on Speedwell Avenue: grocery, fruit, confectionery, barber, tailor, bicycle repair and locksmith. The lower part of the sheet is a separate inset at 100 feet to an inch (Mt. Kemble Avenue and the All Souls Hospital) cut out of this part by a heavy line, and the compass rose stands on the dividing line. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked, with street widths of 50 feet.
notes: Early Street, Atno Avenue, Clinton Street, Clinton Place, Prospect Street and Speedwell Avenue keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
Modern Prospect Street also runs north to Early Street; the sheet draws it only south of Clinton Street, so that junction was left out.
Clinton Place is drawn about 30 feet wide against about 25 feet in the parcels; the junction at Prospect Street is hand-picked.
Part 1 50 ft (Early, Atno, Clinton St/Pl, Prospect, Speedwell); part 2 100 ft strip (Mt Kemble Av, All Souls Hospital), unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: 100 ft strip: Mt. Kemble Avenue, All Souls Hospital (no junction with a modern street; needs carried points from sheet-20 or parcel corners).

sheet-20-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 20 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It lies at the north-west edge of the built-up town. Mt. Kemble Avenue runs across the top from lower left to upper right, and Wetmore Avenue, 66 feet wide, runs parallel to it below. Doughty Street joins them and continues south as Ogden Place, which curves down the right side of the sheet to Miller Road at the foot. Between Mt. Kemble and Wetmore avenues are the blocks numbered 252 and 250 with frame dwellings on deep narrow lots, a veterinary and auto building, wagon sheds and a concrete dwelling drawn in blue. South of Wetmore Avenue the ground is mostly open, with a greenhouse beside Ogden Place and a single large house in block 253. At the foot, an auto and laundry building and other brick buildings stand beside Ogden Place and Miller Road. The lower left corner of the sheet is a boxed inset, a separate part, that shows Ogden Place and Miller Road at a different rotation, and a compass rose with a north arrow stands above it. Water pipes, hydrants, fire alarm boxes and street widths of 40, 50 and 66 feet are marked, and the lettered match-line corners A and B at the edges join the sheet to its neighbours.
notes: Mount Kemble Avenue, Wetmore Avenue, Doughty Street, Ogden Place and Miller Road keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from three junctions along Doughty Street and Ogden Place only (helmert), so low confidence at the left and right edges.
50 ft. Part 1 main (Mt Kemble, Wetmore, Doughty, Ogden Pl), three points nearly in line; part 2 inset Ogden Pl / Miller Rd, anchored.

sheet-20-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 20 is the boxed inset at the lower left corner, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that its north arrow points to the upper right, close to the rotation of the main map. It shows the south end of Ogden Place and Miller Road, which continue the same two streets that meet at the foot of the main part. Ogden Place, 40 feet wide, runs down the page with a slight lean, with Miller Road, 50 feet wide, leaving it to the right near the top. West of Ogden Place are blocks numbered 20 and 253, with a pink brick building with frame wings at the top, a frame dwelling and a half-timber and plastered house. East of Ogden Place lies block 236, with a two-storey dwelling and an auto garage, and a dimension of 200 feet is marked between them. The inset is bounded by a heavy double line on its top and right sides, and a compass rose with a north arrow stands on the dividing line at the top. Water pipes, a hydrant and street widths are marked.
notes: Ogden Place and Miller Road keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
Anchored on the Ogden Place / Miller Road junction with the scale and rotation of the main part; low confidence away from the junction.
50 ft. Part 1 main (Mt Kemble, Wetmore, Doughty, Ogden Pl), three points nearly in line; part 2 inset Ogden Pl / Miller Rd, anchored.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers a residential strip on the western edge of Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right (the printed arrow shows a smaller angle than the street grid fits). Western Avenue crosses the sheet from the upper left to the lower right, a 50 foot street with a four-inch water pipe along it. Lovell, Locust and Searing avenues run up the page from it, and Center Avenue forms a short cross street at the top. Chestnut Street closes the bottom of the sheet and Cherry Street runs down to it from Western Avenue. Fairview Place enters from the right edge. The blocks are numbered 7, 8, 9, 271, 273 and 274, and the neighbouring sheets are 3, 4, 5, 22 and 24 (the sheet numbers printed at the margins). Most of the area is open or thinly built: scattered frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys with small auto sheds, deep lots running back from Western Avenue, and a large unbuilt tract south of the avenue. A wagon and auto shop stands in block 8. The Hillside School, a brick building heated by steam, and a fire gong (locomotive tire) are drawn at the top edge. A brook crosses block 8 and the area beside Searing Avenue, and an old pumping station is marked abandoned on the right. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and the 50 foot street widths are lettered along the streets. A note near the foot says certain dwellings are set 40 feet back from the street line.
notes: Cherry and Chestnut are printed without a suffix; today's streets are Cherry Street and Chestnut Street.
Searing Avenue meets Western Avenue about 10 m from Cherry Street, an offset that the modern street network also shows.
Hillside School stands at the top edge near Center Avenue; the sheet marks an old pumping station as abandoned.
50 ft. Western Av, Center, Locust, Searing, Fairview, Cherry, Chestnut.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 continues the Western Avenue strip of sheet 21 towards the centre of Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Western Avenue crosses the sheet from the left to the lower right edge. Miller Street runs up the page from it and meets Budd Street near the top; Phoenix Avenue leaves Miller Street to the right. Plum Street runs down from Western Avenue towards Chestnut Street, which crosses the lower left corner. Fairview Place comes in from the left and turns into Budd Street at the upper left. Meskill Place is lettered at the right edge just above block 23. The blocks are numbered 5, 272, 273, 274, 420, 430, 431 and 271 and the surrounding sheets are 21, 23 and 24. Dwellings are mostly frame, of two and two and a half storeys, packed along Western Avenue and Phoenix Avenue; much of the ground north of Western Avenue and west of Miller Street is open lots. A brook crosses the sheet from left to right between Budd Street and Western Avenue. A fire alarm box stands on Western Avenue near Miller Street, and a brick dwelling is marked in the lower right. The streets are lettered 50 feet wide, with four, six and eight inch water pipes.
notes: Meskill Place is not in OpenStreetMap and is left out of the configuration.
Plum Street now ends about 25 m short of Chestnut Street.
Budd, Miller and Plum are printed without a suffix; today's streets are Budd Street, Miller Street and Plum Street.
Fairview Place bends into Budd Street at its east end, so that junction is a bend rather than a crossing.
50 ft. Western Av, Miller, Phoenix, Budd, Plum; 4 points; Meskill Pl not in OSM.

sheet-23-1.description: The main part of sheet 23 covers the blocks north-west of the Morristown Green between Budd Street and Cobb Place, from Miller Street on the left to Washington Street at the right edge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Meskill Place runs diagonally across the middle of the part from Miller Street towards Washington Street, and a brook runs parallel to it through the lots south of it. Phoenix Avenue crosses the lower left corner and Lyons Place joins it to Cobb Place. Most of the part is open land: block 430 north of Budd Street and block 426 between Budd Street and Meskill Place are laid out in lots with few buildings. Building is concentrated along Washington Street, with frame dwellings, the wagon sheds and the brick storage warehouse of Bockoven and Day, and along Cobb Place and Phoenix Avenue, where rows of two-storey frame dwellings stand on narrow lots. The Frost Garage, with a cement floor and a gasoline tank, stands near the corner of Cobb Place and Washington Street. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths (50, 40 and 33 feet) are marked. The top of the sheet carries two insets at 100 feet to an inch, which are separate parts.
notes: Meskill Place is not in OpenStreetMap; it has been closed or built over.
Budd, Miller and Washington are Budd Street, Miller Street and Washington Street in OpenStreetMap.

Three parts: 1 main, 50 ft (Budd St to Cobb Pl, Miller St to Washington St; Meskill Pl gone today); 2 inset 100 ft (Milton Pl, Hazlet = Hazlett Street, Kenmuir Av, Mills St); 3 inset 100 ft (Speedwell Av, Kinney, Anderson, Thompson, Frederick; ink 100).

sheet-23-2.description: This inset in the upper left of sheet 23 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows the block bounded by Milton Place, Kenmuir Avenue, Mills Street and Hazlet, in the north-western part of Morristown, with north to the upper right. Block 445 is only partly built: frame dwellings of one and a half to two storeys stand along Milton Place and along Hazlet, with a produce storage building and sheds on the Kenmuir Avenue side, and the centre of the block is open. East of Kenmuir Avenue a strip of block 446 shows further dwellings on lots facing Kenmuir Avenue. Four-inch water pipes run in Milton Place, Hazlet and Kenmuir Avenue and a six-inch pipe in Mills, with hydrants at the corners and the street widths of 50 feet marked.
notes: Hazlet is Hazlett Street in OpenStreetMap; Mills is Mills Street.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch although the main part of the sheet is at 50 feet.

Three parts: 1 main, 50 ft (Budd St to Cobb Pl, Miller St to Washington St; Meskill Pl gone today); 2 inset 100 ft (Milton Pl, Hazlet = Hazlett Street, Kenmuir Av, Mills St); 3 inset 100 ft (Speedwell Av, Kinney, Anderson, Thompson, Frederick; ink 100).

sheet-23-3.description: This inset in the upper middle of sheet 23 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows Speedwell Avenue north of Frederick between Kinney and Thompson, with north pointing to the upper left. Block 351, bounded by Speedwell Avenue, Kinney, Anderson and Thompson, is filled with small frame dwellings on narrow lots running back from Anderson. South of Thompson, block 352 has dwellings along Speedwell Avenue and a bakery with its mixing room and ovens; east of Anderson, block 56 has a few more dwellings. West of Speedwell Avenue is open land in block 370 with a single outbuilding, and Frederick enters at the bottom left. Water pipes of four and eight inches are marked in the streets, and Speedwell Avenue is given as 66 feet wide.
notes: Kinney, Anderson, Thompson and Frederick are Kinney Street, Anderson Street, Thompson Street and Frederick Street in OpenStreetMap.
Detected with ink_below_paper 100: the 100 ft line work is lighter than on the 50 ft sheets.

Three parts: 1 main, 50 ft (Budd St to Cobb Pl, Miller St to Washington St; Meskill Pl gone today); 2 inset 100 ft (Milton Pl, Hazlet = Hazlett Street, Kenmuir Av, Mills St); 3 inset 100 ft (Speedwell Av, Kinney, Anderson, Thompson, Frederick; ink 100).

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 shows the west side of the Morris County courthouse district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Phoenix Avenue and Western Avenue run side by side from the left edge to the right, with block 420 between them. Cobb Place closes the top, Lyons Place runs down at the upper left, and Washington Street runs diagonally down the right side with Atno Avenue entering at the right edge. Ann Street runs down the page from Western Avenue to Court Street at the foot. Dwellings are frame houses of two and two and a half storeys along both avenues and Washington Street, with some brick dwellings at the left. The Y.M.C.A. building at the lower right, drawn in brick with a swimming pool, gymnasium, bowling alleys and class rooms, and the Morris County Buildings at the lower right corner, with the jail and the vault of the county offices on Court Lane, are the principal institutions. A distributing reservoir with a capacity of one million gallons stands in block 422, beside the curved edge of Fort Nonsense Park at the lower left. Blocks 420 to 424 are numbered, and the neighbouring sheets are 1, 2, 22, 23 and 26. Water pipes of three to ten inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked.
notes: Washington, Ann and Court are printed without a suffix; today's streets are Washington Street, Ann Street and Court Street.
The Morris County Buildings and the Y.M.C.A. building are drawn at the lower right.
Western Avenue and Washington Street meet just beyond the right edge, about 6 m off the sheet.
50 ft. Phoenix, Western, Washington, Cobb, Lyons, Ann, Court; courthouse, Fort Nonsense Park.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 shows a district north of the Morris County courthouse, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Washington Street runs down the left edge. Colonial Road crosses the upper part from the left to the right edge, Knox Road enters from Washington Street at mid height, and Mills Street runs along the foot of the sheet. Brewster Place and Early Street run between them, Early Street curving to the lower right edge, and Hazlet Street is lettered along the right edge. Budd Street is named at the lower left corner. The blocks are numbered 410, 440, 441, 442, 443 and 444; neighbouring sheets are 8, 23, 26 and 27. Much of the ground is open and divided into long unbuilt lots, especially between Colonial Road and Mills Street. Frame dwellings, several of them stuccoed, stand along Washington Street and the lower edge of Mills Street, with sheds and auto buildings behind. Mills Street Public School, a brick building, stands at the lower right between Early and Hazlet streets. Two brooks run through the sheet, one beside Knox Road and one crossing Mills Street. A dwelling marked C.B. (concrete block) stands in block 442. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches and the 50 foot street widths are lettered.
notes: Hazlet is today's Hazlett Street.
Washington, Early and Mills are printed without a suffix; today's streets are Washington Street, Early Street and Mills Street.
Modern Brewster Place is a short stub from Colonial Road; Knox Road no longer reaches Brewster Place.
Mills Street Public School is drawn at the lower right.
50 ft. Colonial Rd, Knox Rd, Brewster Pl, Early, Mills, Hazlet (= Hazlett Street), Washington.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows the Morristown High School area on the northern side of the courthouse district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right, with the printed arrow tilted slightly upward. Washington Street runs down the left edge and Early Street down the right. Atno Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet from the lower left to the right edge, with Clinton Street branching from its south side. Harrison Street leaves Early Street at the right edge, and Meskill Place is lettered at the left edge near block 23. A long brook runs through the middle of the sheet from top to bottom and crosses Atno Avenue. The central ground, block 410, is open land. Frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys line Washington Street, among them a radiator and welding works with a cement floor at the lower left, and similar dwellings, some brick veneered, line Early Street. The High School, built in 1918, is the main building: a large brick structure at the lower right corner of the block, heated by steam, lit by electricity, with a gymnasium, stage, auditorium and balcony, a manual training room, reinforced concrete floors and roof and exposed steel beams. Sheets 2, 19, 23, 24, 25 and 27 are printed at the margins. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches and the 50 foot street widths are marked.
notes: Meskill Place is not in OpenStreetMap and is left out of the configuration.
Washington and Early are printed without a suffix; today's streets are Washington Street and Early Street.
The High School is dated 1918 on the sheet.
50 ft. High School; Washington, Early, Atno, Clinton, Harrison; three points (exact fit).

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the district north of Early Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing nearly straight up. Mills Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the top, a 60 foot avenue lined by frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys. Kenmuir Avenue enters from the left edge and Hazlet Street from the left near the lower left corner. Harrison Street runs from Early Street at the foot up to the top of the sheet, parallel to Mills Street, with Morton Street and Grant Street crossing it to the right. Cleveland Street and Bellevue Terrace run down the right edge. Early Street closes the foot of the sheet. The blocks are numbered 401 to 404, 411, 446 and 448, and the neighbouring sheets are 23, 25, 26, 28 and 29. The blocks between Mills Street and Harrison Street are densely built with frame dwellings, many with stables, auto sheds and small shops. Several dwellings are marked concrete block, three dwellings with brick first storeys stand near Bellevue Terrace, and a pipe shop and plumbing premises are drawn near Early Street. The ground west of Mills Street and north of Kenmuir Avenue is open lots. Four and eight inch water pipes, fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked, with street widths of 40 and 50 feet.
notes: Hazlet is today's Hazlett Street, and Belleview Terrace is today's Bellevue Terrace.

Mills, Harrison, Morton, Grant, Cleveland and Early are printed without a suffix; today's streets are Mills Street, Harrison Street, Morton Street, Grant Street, Cleveland Street or Avenue and Early Street.
50 ft. Mills, Harrison, Kenmuir, Morton, Grant, Hazlet, Early; Belleview Ter (= Bellevue Terrace).

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers a residential and light commercial district on the north-west side of Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned slightly from north. Sussex Avenue crosses the sheet from the upper left to the middle right, meeting Speedwell Avenue, which runs down the right side to Early Street along the bottom edge. Cleveland Street bounds block 406 at upper left, Grant Street and Columbia Street run roughly east and west between blocks 406, 405 and 401, and Belleview Terrace runs down the left side. Most lots carry two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings, with narrow deep lots in blocks 405 and 406. Block 406 contains the greenhouses of Geo. Bird, florist, and a junk yard on Cleveland Street. At the junction of Sussex and Speedwell Avenues a pink brick building holds the Flatiron Garage of W. D. Marshall, with printing, auto repairing and other uses marked inside it. St. Margaret's R. C. Church and St. Margaret's School occupy the large open block 401 south of Columbia Street, and Orion N. Hughson, undertaker, and several auto shops and repair garages line Speedwell Avenue below them. A scale bar stands in the lower margin and a compass rose at upper right. Block 408 lies north-east of Sussex Avenue and Vail Place enters Speedwell Avenue from the right. Adjoining sheets are numbered 27, 29, 30, 15 and 19 in the margins.
notes: Belleview Terrace is Bellevue Terrace in OpenStreetMap; Cleveland, Grant, Columbia, Henry and Early are Cleveland Street, Grant Street, Columbia Street, Henry Street and Early Street.
The Flatiron Garage building (W. D. Marshall) fills the triangle between Sussex Avenue and Speedwell Avenue.
50 ft. Cleveland, Grant, Sussex, Columbia, Belleview Ter, Speedwell, Early.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the north-western edge of built-up Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 6 degrees from north. Two wide streets dominate it: Sussex Avenue, drawn 66 feet wide, runs from the upper left corner to the lower right, and Mills Street crosses it from the lower left to the top near the middle, meeting Cutler Street at the top and Speedwell Place to the right. The whole left half of the sheet is block 392, a large undrawn tract of open land crossed only by faint property lines and carrying the compass rose. Development lies in the blocks east of Mills Street and south-east of Sussex Avenue. Block 394, between Cutler Street and Sussex Avenue, has three frame dwellings and an auto shed. Block 390 and block 391 east of Mills Street hold dwellings and the greenhouses of the Thos. Holton Estate, with glass roofs and a house for the grower. Block 393 along the south side of Sussex Avenue is a row of deep lots with two-storey dwellings, a wagon shed and stables, and small auto houses, and ends at the corner of Cleveland Street at the lower right, where several narrow houses front the street. Blocks 31, 32, 30, 28 and 27 are named in the margins for the neighbouring sheets, and Elliott Street and Ralph Place are lettered where they enter the top of the sheet. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets.
notes: Cutler, Mills and Cleveland are Cutler Street, Mills Street and Cleveland Street in OpenStreetMap.
Sussex Avenue is drawn 66 feet wide; Mills Street 50 feet.
50 ft. Sussex Av, Mills, Cutler, Speedwell Pl; large open block 392.

sheet-30-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 30 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 7 degrees from north, along Speedwell Avenue in north-western Morristown. Speedwell Avenue, drawn 66 feet wide, crosses the sheet from top to bottom, with Cutler Street, Speedwell Place, Lakeside Place, Logan Place, Henry Street and Vail Place meeting it from the sides. The left half shows blocks 390 and 391, mainly frame dwellings with a few auto sheds, a cement and metal company at the left edge, and the pink brick Speedwell Avenue Public School, heated by steam and warm air and lit by electricity, between Speedwell Place and Henry Street. Sussex Avenue and the end of Cleveland Street enter at the lower left. East of Speedwell Avenue the sheet is mostly open land in blocks 340 and 343, with a few small buildings, one marked as a grocery, and an auto shed north of Speedwell Place. Block 342 between Lakeside Place and Logan Place is built up with a row of attached two and a half storey dwellings facing Speedwell Avenue and detached cement block houses along Lakeside Place. Pocahontas Street bounds the block on the east, and Pocahontas Lake with its stream runs down the right edge. Two insets are cut out of the sheet: a rectangle at the upper right (part 2: Speedwell Avenue and block 409 south of Vail Place) and one at the lower left (part 3: Logan Place and Pocahontas Lake). Adjoining sheets are named 29, 28, 32, 15 and 30 in the margins.
notes: Cutler, Henry and Pocahontas are Cutler Street, Henry Street and Pocahontas Street in OpenStreetMap; Cleveland Street is lettered only in part at the lower left.
Speedwell Avenue is drawn 66 feet wide.
The Speedwell Avenue Public School stands on the west side of Speedwell Avenue between Speedwell Place and Henry Street.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Speedwell Av, Cutler to Vail Pl); 2 inset upper right (Speedwell Av south of Vail Pl), anchored on a parcel block corner; 3 inset lower left (Logan Pl / Pocahontas St), anchored on parcel corners.

sheet-30-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 30 is an inset at the upper right, ruled off by a heavy line and drawn at what appears to be the same 50 feet to an inch, with its own north arrow pointing straight up. It shows Speedwell Avenue running down its left edge and block 409 to the east, entered from Vail Place at the top. The inset continues the ground south of Vail Place that the neighbouring sheet 28 leaves blank beside Speedwell Avenue, and the block numbers 28, 30 and 15 refer to adjoining sheets. The block holds a handful of dwellings along Speedwell Avenue, a synagogue near the middle, and an auto repairing shop in blue with a long carpenter shop and shed beside it. A pink brick building, probably a factory or storage building, stands at the bottom of the inset. The street frontage is lined with house numbers from 159 to 185 and water pipes of 8 inches are marked along Speedwell Avenue. A lot line sketches the open back land to the east, and the sheet number 30 is printed in the corner.
notes: The inset is rotated about 14 degrees from the main map of sheet 30 although its printed arrow points straight up; it is placed from one block corner and is low confidence.
A synagogue is lettered on the block.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Speedwell Av, Cutler to Vail Pl); 2 inset upper right (Speedwell Av south of Vail Pl), anchored on a parcel block corner; 3 inset lower left (Logan Pl / Pocahontas St), anchored on parcel corners.

sheet-30-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 30 is a small inset at the lower left, ruled off by a heavy line and drawn at about 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows the eastern end of Logan Place, where it runs across Pocahontas Street, with block 343 to the south and Pocahontas Lake and its stream to the east. It continues the ground east of the main map, beyond the Pocahontas Street end of Logan Place. The only buildings are a two storey dwelling with a cement block first floor, house numbers 25, on Logan Place and a small structure marked as vacant, on brick piles, near the lake edge. A hydrant stands on Pocahontas Street and water pipes of 4 inches and 30 foot street widths are marked. Pocahontas Lake runs diagonally across the right side of the inset with its flow shown by an arrow, and block 30 is named in the lower margin for the neighbouring sheet.
notes: Pocahontas Street is lettered 'Pocahontas St.' on this inset and 'Pocahontas' on the main map.
The part is placed from two parcel corners of the Logan Place and Pocahontas Street junction, with the scale and north taken from the main map; low confidence.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Speedwell Av, Cutler to Vail Pl); 2 inset upper right (Speedwell Av south of Vail Pl), anchored on a parcel block corner; 3 inset lower left (Logan Pl / Pocahontas St), anchored on parcel corners.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the north-western fringe of Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 25 degrees from north. A curved Lake Road forms the left edge. Elliott Street runs up the left-centre of the sheet from Sussex Avenue at the bottom to Walker Avenue, a 50 foot street that curves away to the right towards Mills Street at the right edge. Ralph Place crosses the middle from Walker Avenue down to Cutler Street, which cuts across the lower right to Mills Street. The upper centre and right are mostly open land in block 382, crossed by a few lot lines, with only a stuccoed dwelling and a cement block auto shed near the right edge. Blocks 383 and 384 on either side of Elliott Street, left of the sheet, are laid out in long narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings and a few auto sheds, one cement block dwelling and a foundation outline. A wedge-shaped block 385 lies between Elliott Street and Ralph Place and holds a house marked Knollcroft, built of terra cotta tile, with other dwellings and auto sheds. Block 386, to the right of Ralph Place, has a row of dwellings along Mills Street, several of them terra cotta tile or stucco, with house numbers 105 to 130. The compass rose stands in the open ground at the top. Blocks 388, 29 and 32 are named in the margins for adjoining sheets, and water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked.
notes: Elliott, Walker, Cutler and Mills are Elliott Street, Walker Avenue, Cutler Street and Mills Street in OpenStreetMap.
Lake Road is not used as control because it is curved and runs off the sheet.
50 ft. Lake Rd, Elliott, Walker, Ralph Pl, Cutler, Mills; mostly open.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers a mostly undeveloped part of north-western Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees from north. Frederick Street runs along the top, Cutler Street along the bottom, Mills Street down the left edge and Speedwell Avenue down the right. Walker Avenue crosses the middle from Mills Street to Speedwell Avenue, and Condict Place runs from Frederick Street to Walker Avenue between blocks 381 and 380. Blocks 381 and 380, north of Walker Avenue, are laid out in long narrow lots, almost all vacant; the exceptions are a pair of attached dwellings and a few frame houses and auto sheds, and, at the Walker Avenue end of block 380, a cluster of dwellings and the L. B. Weeks Dairy, a small building in blue with steam heat and electric light. Block 387, south of Walker Avenue, holds a row of narrow lots along Walker Avenue, larger lots with a few big frame dwellings and sheds in the middle, and several stuccoed houses near Cutler Street. A strip of block 340 along the right edge, beyond Speedwell Avenue, has a close row of dwellings with a pink brick building, house numbers running from 204 to 285, and the Speedwell Avenue Chapel near the bottom, heated by furnace and lit by electricity. The compass rose sits over Frederick Street at the top. Blocks 370, 23, 31, 29 and 30 are named in the margins for adjoining sheets.
notes: Frederick, Mills and Cutler are Frederick Street, Mills Street and Cutler Street in OpenStreetMap.
Speedwell Avenue Chapel and the L. B. Weeks Dairy are named buildings on the sheet.
50 ft. Frederick, Condict Pl, Walker Av, Mills, Speedwell, Cutler.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers a residential district on the south side of Morristown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 49 degrees from north, so that north points to the upper right. South Street, drawn 66 feet wide, runs down the left side, with James Street entering from the left near the top. Franklin Street runs roughly parallel to it through the centre and turns south-east at the bottom, while Franklin Place leaves it to the right near the middle of the sheet. Altamont Court runs down the right edge. Block 150 and 151, between South Street and Franklin Street, are filled with large frame dwellings on deep lots, many of two and a half storeys with outbuildings; the largest holds a barn, storage building and auto sheds, and a dwelling lettered Maple Lawn stands at the top. South of them block 152 is nearly empty, with a few houses at the foot of the sheet. East of Franklin Street, blocks 172, 174 and 175 hold detached frame dwellings on narrower lots, with a small pink brick building at the edge of block 172 near Altamont Court, and a fire alarm box at the corner of Franklin Place. The compass rose with its long needle stands at the top right. Blocks 10, 11, 34, 37 and 38 are named in the margins for the adjoining sheets, and a street lettered Fo. enters at the lower right corner. Hydrants and water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked along the streets.
notes: South, Franklin and James are South Street, Franklin Street and James Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from only two street junctions (James and South, Franklin Place and Franklin Street); low confidence.
A street lettered only as Fo. at the lower right corner is cut off by the sheet edge and is not listed as a street name; it is probably Ford Avenue.
50 ft. South St, Franklin St, Franklin Pl, James, Altamont Ct; two-point helmert.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers the edge of Morristown where Hill Street bends past the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Hill Street, 50 to 60 feet wide, enters at the top, swings to the left around block 173 and meets Franklin Place and, at the bottom, Ford Avenue. West of it lie blocks 171, 174 and 175, built up with two and three storey frame dwellings, garages and a stuccoed house, with Altamont Court running into the block at the upper left as a short court with its own corner radius. East of Hill Street, block 173 is open ground with a row of dwellings along its southern end and a compass rose in its blank middle. The railroad crosses the sheet from top to bottom on the right and Ford Avenue passes over it at the foot. Beside the tracks stands the coal and wood yard of Pruden and Burke Co. Inc., with coal pockets, a grain elevator, a saw mill with electric motor, a kindling wood factory, wagon sheds, an office and a gasoline tank. A lumber storage yard with curved dashed lines occupies the top of block 173. A brook runs down the right edge and under Ford Avenue. Morris Street and Ridgedale Avenue appear at the top right corner. The dashed line across the top is the Morristown boundary, with its corner letters A and B.
notes: Hill Street is Hill Street in OpenStreetMap; Franklin Place and Ford Avenue keep their names.

Georeferenced on two junctions along Hill Street (Franklin Place and Ford Avenue); the third, Morris Street and Ridgedale Avenue, lies just beyond the top edge. The Ford Avenue crossing of the railroad is a bridge in OpenStreetMap and gave no control point.
50 ft. Hill St, Franklin Pl, Ford Av, Morris, Ridgedale Av; two-point helmert.

sheet-35-1.description: The main part of sheet 35, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right, lies north and west of the Morristown Green along Morris Street. Morris Street runs down the left edge from Olyphant Place at the top, past Ridgedale Avenue, and bends south east at Ford Avenue to become Morris Avenue, which carries on to the lower edge beside Washington Avenue. Ridgedale Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally to the right, lined with narrow lots of dwellings, and meets Abbet Avenue and the street labelled Whippany at the Morris and Somerset Electric Co. power station, a large brick plant with boiler house and engine room, and the nearby Goodman Bros. muslin underwear factory. Olyphant Place and the curving Olyphant Drive and Parkway lie across the top, with block 120 of dwellings between them and Ridgedale Avenue. A stream crosses the middle of the sheet. South of it, blocks 183 and 281 are mostly open land cut by Lafayette Avenue and Division, with the Washington Headquarters buildings, the Cottage and other estate houses inside block 183. Washington Place curves round the south east, and the Whippany River forms a loop in the lower right. The lower right corner, drawn off a heavy line and showing Ford Avenue, Morris and Howell Lane, is a separate area and is not part of this mask.
notes: Abbet Avenue is Abbett Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the street labelled Whippany at the power station is Legion Place.
Olyphant Drive and Parkway are Olyphant Drive and Olyphant Parkway; Lafayette Avenue and Division as drawn do not exist now.
The drawn junction of Ford Avenue and Morris at the left was not used: the modern node lies about 30 m from it.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 shows the country south east of the Green, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right. Morris Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet to a fork, where Columbia Road leaves to the south west and Whippany Road to the south east. Washington Avenue crosses the upper left diagonally from the top edge to the left edge. Between Washington Avenue and Olmstead Road lies the Parkway, a curved private road with a loop and branch road at the top, laid out around The Georgian Gardens Inc. and the estate Fair Oaks, whose main building and a small lodge are coloured blue. Block 72 is divided into long narrow lots on both sides of the Parkway. Olmstead Road curves from the left edge round the foot of the estate to Columbia Road, passing the H. M. Olmstead Estate, and a pond lies below it. East of Morris Avenue are large properties, among them Rest Harrow, Mrs. Fayette Smith, Egerton Brown, The Anchorage and Penllyn, mostly frame dwellings with stables and outbuildings drawn in yellow and pink. Ford Farm and the Nicholas Marinaro premises, with a greenhouse, appear on the open land at the left. A compass rose and the scale note stand at the top right.
notes: Olmstead Road, Washington Avenue and the Parkway (modern Georgian Road) survive; the drawn Columbia Road is today the line of Morris Avenue and the fork has been remodelled.
The Normandy Heights development has since replaced most of the estates shown.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers the district south west of the Morristown Green around the junction of South Street and Madison Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. South Street runs from the top of the sheet down the left side and out at the lower left, and Headley Road enters from the left at the top. Madison Avenue leaves South Street at a fork near the top, runs south east across the middle and leaves at the lower right. Ford Avenue sweeps in a wide curve across the upper right to Franklin Avenue, with Jefferson Avenue crossing from Madison Avenue to the right edge and a corner of Vine Street at the bottom left. The land is mostly large estates with houses, stables, greenhouses and a few service buildings: Mrs. Geo. W. Jenkins, the Andrew Cobb Estate, Mary E. Richardson, Armanda E. Whitnall, F. W. Perkins, Letchford Estate, Margaret S. Colgate, D. H. McAlpin, Benj. F. Evans, Dayton R. Minard, Geo. E. Chisolm, Geo. C. Fraser, Lorraine W. Mellon and others. Frame dwellings predominate, with a few brick or stucco ones in pink, and a fire alarm box at the top and lower right. A compass rose stands near the top right.
notes: The drawn Ford Avenue is today partly Revere Road; Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street.
Jefferson Avenue as drawn does not appear in OpenStreetMap.
Only three control points, two of them hand-picked on curved or forked junctions (Madison Avenue with South Street, Ford Avenue with Franklin Street); low confidence.

sheet-38-1.description: The main part of sheet 38 follows Madison Avenue south east of the Green, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right and slightly down. Madison Avenue runs down the middle from the top to the junction with Franklin Avenue and Canfield Road, then continues, bending to the lower left at Normandie Parkway, where a concrete bridge carries the road over the railroad. Canfield Road enters from the upper left; Franklin Avenue runs from the junction to the right and then turns north east along the right side. Washington Avenue crosses the lower right beyond the railroad, which runs diagonally with several tracks. The land is divided into large estate blocks numbered 40, 41, 50, 51, 52 and 61, with scattered dwellings, a greenhouse and outbuildings: Ransom H. Thomas, Elizabeth Day, Gertrude L. Thebaud, Woodbury G. Langdon Co. Inc., E. W. Coggeshall, the John D. Canfield Estate, Benj. F. Evans and the George G. Kip Place. Gardener's Cottage is marked at the left. A compass rose stands at the top right. A heavy-bordered inset at the upper left, showing South Street and carrying the sheet labels 10, 33 and 37, is a separate part and is cut out of this mask.
notes: The drawn Canfield Road is today Turtle Road; Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street; Normandie Parkway is Normandy Parkway.
The junction of Madison Avenue and Normandy Parkway is not used: the modern node lies about 27 m from the drawn one.

sheet-39-1.description: The main part of sheet 39 lies south east of the Green on the country road to Convent, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Madison Avenue enters at the top right and runs south, curving, along the right edge, and is crossed by Glen Road near the middle, where the road jogs slightly at Madison Avenue. The remainder is large estate ground, mostly open: H. O. Bates, John I. Waterbury with his house Fairfield, Josephine B. Garretson, Est. with Sunny Mede, John A. Stewart, E. F. Waterbury, E. W. Coggeshall and A. Fillmore Hyde, whose house Seldomere stands at the lower left. Dwellings are frame with a few brick or stucco ones in pink, with stables, auto garages and a cluster of outbuildings near the top. Blocks are numbered 20, 85, 87, 88 and 332. A compass rose with north toward the upper right stands in the open land at the top right, and a note beside Madison Avenue gives the distance of 930 feet to Township Road, shown on the inset above. The top left inset and the lower strip with South Street are separate parts and are cut out of this mask.
notes: Glen Road is Old Glen Road in OpenStreetMap, meeting Madison Avenue at the Kahn Road junction.

sheet-39-2.description: The inset at the upper left of sheet 39 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, pointing nearly straight up, and is bordered by a heavy line. It shows Madison Avenue running down the middle, a main road 60 to 70 feet wide with house numbers in the 1600s, crossed near the top by Township Road, which leaves it to the left. Most of the area is open estate land in blocks 85, 86 and 87, with large properties including the Morris County Golf Club clubhouse at the top, Gen. E. P. Meany's Alnwick Hall, with its pink brick house, stable, auto garage and outbuildings, and a house and sheds near the left edge. Dashed lines mark water mains of six inches along Township Road and Madison Avenue, with tank notes of 300 and 180 gallons. A note near the top reads 350 feet to Fr. D. See below, and the margins are marked No Exposure where the sheet adjoins no other building. The inset continues the line of Madison Avenue south of the main part of the sheet, which carries a note giving 930 feet to Township Road.
